C-19.Name: Heading navigation: Go-to-Heading palette (Cmd+T) + active-heading highlight in the TOC (matrix P1)
C-19.Summary: Long agent-generated documents need heading navigation parity with VS Code. C-19 v1 ships two pieces over the existing listToc/slug infrastructure: (1) a Go-to-Heading command palette (Cmd+T — the VS Code workspace-symbol binding, free in both the native menu and the registry) fuzzy-searching the active document's headings and jumping via the established scroll-to-header slugs; (2) the sidebar TOC highlights the heading the viewport is currently in (the "where am I" half of the breadcrumb idea). Title-bar heading breadcrumbs are an explicit follow-up (the C-9 title-clearance geometry deserves its own change), not v1.

Problem.Description: Navigating a 2000-line agent-written strategy doc requires scrolling or eyeballing the TOC; there is no keyboard symbol-search and the TOC does not show which section the viewport is in.
Problem.RootCause: The quick-open command searches files only; the TOC renders a flat tree with no active-node tracking; no heading search existed upstream (matrix: "Go-to-header / workspace symbol search ❌").
Problem.Evidence: docs/research/markdown-feature-matrix.md Editing & structure row (P1, small effort); commands/quickOpen.js is the palette-command pattern (search/executeSubcommand); sideBar/toc.vue renders listToc via el-tree with no active state; editor.vue already owns scroll-to-header → scrollToElement('#slug'); Cmd+T is bound nowhere (menu + registry grep clean).

Goals.R-1: Go-to-Heading palette command 'edit.go-to-heading' (Cmd+T, native menu entry in the Find/navigation neighborhood): fuzzy-filters the ACTIVE document's listToc headings (level shown as indentation), Enter jumps via bus scroll-to-header slug; empty list when the document has no headings; untitled tabs behave the same (TOC is content-based).
Goals.R-2: Active-heading highlight in the sidebar TOC: the heading containing the current viewport top (recomputed on muya scroll events, debounced, fixed 80px activation band) gets a distinct style; the highlight follows both reading and editing; clicking nodes keeps the existing jump behavior.
Goals.R-3: No regressions to the palette (file quick-open untouched), the TOC click-to-jump, or the C-9 title-bar geometry (untouched — breadcrumbs are a follow-up change).

Constraints.Constraint: No new dependencies; reuses listToc, slugs, command-palette and el-tree.
menu-consistency: Cmd+T shortcut ⇒ native menu entry (or allowlist — menu entry preferred for discoverability).
Active-heading recomputation is passive (scroll listener only, debounced) — no muya core changes.
Scoped 100% coverage of new command/TOC logic; e2e visual gate (palette lists headings, jump scrolls; TOC highlight follows scroll); grace lint zero findings; two sequential reviews.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Workspace-wide (all-files) heading search — active document v1.
Title-bar heading breadcrumbs (C-9 clearance geometry — separate change).
Folding, split view, relative-path autocomplete (other P1 items).

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Unit: HeadingSearchCommand search filters listToc (fuzzy + level indent in the label), executeSubcommand emits scroll-to-header with the slug, empty-TOC documents return []; command registered with the Cmd+T accelerator + native menu id pinned.
Unit + e2e: TOC active node recomputes on scroll (debounced listener), only one node highlighted at a time, click-to-jump unchanged.
Full suite green; grace lint zero findings on changed files; two sequential reviews clean.

AffectedAreas.M-011: palette command + editor wiring (heading search, active-heading tracking)

C-19.VerificationIntent: Unit: heading-search command table tests; TOC active-node component tests. Visual e2e: palette → heading → scroll lands the heading in the viewport; TOC highlight moves with scrolling. Governance: V-M-011 scenario + commands at implementation time; menu-consistency pin.
